claims.text: A neural-network potential can be trained on a sparse set of ab initio molecular-dynamics configurations to evaluate high-temperature free energies.
Perturbative corrections can restore vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling contributions missing from the ML potential.
The proposed method can reproduce the full free-energy landscapes of both solid and liquid states at high temperatures.
The proposed method can substantially reduce computational cost relative to explicit ab initio MD and TOR-TILD.
The cost reduction and fidelity are expected to extend to multicomponent high-entropy systems.
The ML model acts as a surrogate representation of the potential-energy surface.
Targeted perturbative corrections mediate recovery of anharmonic and electron–vibration free-energy contributions.
ML interpolation of the free-energy surface bypasses exhaustive ab initio MD sampling.
Reintroducing vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling through corrections maintains intrinsic free-energy fidelity at reduced cost.
The proposed workflow will provide roughly a 10-fold computational speedup.
The proposed workflow will predict fusion properties and related thermodynamic observables without significant loss of fidelity relative to explicit ab initio MD or TOR-TILD.
The method is applicable near fusion conditions where both solid and liquid phase space is represented in the training data.
The proposed applicability spans elemental, binary, and high-entropy alloy systems.
The method should work when anharmonic and electron–vibration contributions are moderate enough to be treated accurately by perturbative corrections.
Systems with unusually strong anharmonicity or bonding environments outside the training distribution may fall outside the method's valid regime.
A decisive benchmark should compare solid and liquid phase free energies, melting temperature, latent heat, and computational cost against explicit ab initio MD or TOR-TILD.
The hypothesis is to be rejected if errors exceed a predefined acceptable margin or if the workflow does not approach a 10-fold cost reduction.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and predicted outcome treat explicit ab initio MD and TOR-TILD as distinct comparison workflows, whereas the baseline describes explicit ab initio MD free-energy evaluations 'with TOR-TILD,' partially conflating the two baselines.
